newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index edges up at noon, but fall likely.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index edges up at noon, but fall likely.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index inched higher at midday on Wednesday, but is expected to fall in the afternoon led by companies which posted poor 1996 results, analysts said.
Several firms which issued their annual reports today, with shares suspended in the morning, are expected to come under heavy selling pressure due to their weak results, they said.
The foreign currency B index gained 0.05 points or 0.03 percent to 175.95 on turnover of HK$56.87 million.
"Substantial losses are expected in companies that issued poor results for 1996, which is likely to drag down the index in the afternoon," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
"The index fluctuated in the morning as investors held back ahead of the holiday," he said.
The Shenzhen and Shanghai stock markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for the official Labour Day holiday and will open again on Monday.
Shenzhen Tellus Holdings Co Ltd, Hainan Pearl River Enterprises Holdings Ltd and Gintian Industry (Group) Co Ltd all posted losses for 1996 on Wednesday.
A handful of other B share companies announced weaker 1996 earnings.
"But sharp falls are unlikely as investors had been expecting the announcement of poor performances by these companies," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Analysts said the index will maintain an upward trend in the short- to medium-term.
"Everything is clearer now as all companies have announced their annual results," the Guotai analyst said.
Anhui Gujing Distillery was the best performer, gaining HK$0.50 or 4.55 percent to HK$11.50.
The A share index lost 1.66 points or 0.34 percent to close the morning at 483.06 on turnover of 4.78 billion yuan.
Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate was the biggest loser on the A share market, plunging 0.69 yuan or 6.34 percent to 10.20 yuan.
